text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- The cabinet decided on a comprehensive reform of the judicial system, establishing a Hungarian Jewish Heritage Foundation and ordered the finance minister to begin talks with Postabank executives on granting a subordinated loan.

- Hungarian officials attempted Thursday to point out to 15 judges from the International Court of Justice in the Hague the environmental damage caused on the Hungarian side of the Danube by the Gabcikovo hydroelectric power project in Slovakia.
- President Arpad Goncz and his entourage arrived in Brasilia Thursday.
- The Public Procurement Council imposed a HUF 20 million fine on the Defence Ministry Procurement Office Thursday for what it described as irregular handling of a recent missile tender.
- A motion for the dismissal from her post of Deputy Speaker Agnes Nagy Maczo will not be submitted to Parliament as no consensus was reached at a meeting of the House Committee.
- The Agricultural Producers' Advocacy Organisation will stage a mass rally in Budapest today to be followed by a rally of Istvan Csurka's Hungarian Justice and Life Party.
- The rate of unemployment stands at 11 percent.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- A senior Foreign Ministry official said it is practically fixed that Hungary, along with other Central and East European countries, will begin NATO accession talks after the Madrid summit of the alliance in July.
- February industrial production increased by 7.8 percent compared to the same month in 1996.
- Two trade association have appealed to the Constitutional Court against limitations on cash payment that will take effect July 1.
- Eximbank is likely to extend a loan to Brazilian companies to cover 85 percent of the $120 million value of Hungarian goods shipments to Brazil.
- Two Creditanstalt funds, one investing in Hungarian state securities and the other in shares, will be merged in the near future.
- The chemical giant BorsodChem has increased the equities of two subsidiaries, the shrink-wrap manufacturer and trader Ongropack Kft. and BC-KC Formalin Kft.

- Hungarian and foreign experts, government specialists on minority policy and media from 17 countries are attending a two-day international conference entitled Minorities and the Media, which opened in Budapest on Thursday.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea welcomed Budapest Mayor Gabor Demszky in Bucharest on Thursday.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The pension and health care social security funds accumulated a 10.2 billion forints loss in the first two months of 1997, according to preliminary calculations.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Accession to the EU would increase the annual rate of GDP growth in East European countries by 0.5 percent on average, concludes a study by the German economic research firm DIW.
- The price of shares in the Budapest electricity works Elmu went up by some 10 percent on the OTC market in the past week and reached its nominal value yesterday.
- The insurance firm Providencia Rt. generated after-tax profits of 465 million forints last year.
- The sum managed by the pension fund of the insurance firm AB Aegon went up by 52 percent in the past three months.
